summary: Mars Walk Mission lets you walk across real Martian terrain in VR. Built from NASA, USGS and ESA data, it follows Perseverance’s path through Jezero Crater and lets you plan a route on foot, check the conditions at your location, and stand at the Bunsen Peak sample site, where we recreated the drill hole left by Perseverance’s 24th sample. It is a hackathon prototype made for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
details:
What it does and how it works. A Python generator turns orbital data into a scene, and a Godot viewer lets the explorer walk through it. The map combines data sources at different resolutions: terrain (HiRISE, 1 m), orthophoto (25 cm), and horizon (CTX, HRSC+MOLA). Detail is highest at the point of interest, while the rest of the map stays lighter to keep performance.

Point of interest: Bunsen Peak. We recreated the Bunsen Peak rock as a simplified model, then applied a filter based on an image from Perseverance’s WATSON camera, so its texture and appearance resemble the real rock. Using the angle and cut data from Perseverance’s drill, we also recreated, at full scale, the hole left after the sample was removed.

Navigation. Our algorithm calculates the best approximate route between any two points on Mars. We map the terrain into a positional matrix and assign each cell a value, from positive to negative, based on its slope and terrain type.

Atmosphere. This layer shows pressure, dust opacity, radiation, oxygen and temperature at the explorer’s location. Baseline values come from NASA rover instruments (MEDA, RAD and SAM). They are presented as a panel, five false-color views, haze, and sound.

Map design. The map is based on the distance Perseverance has traveled over 5 years, so the route follows the rover’s real path across Jezero Crater. Sol markers, one for each Martian day, are placed at their correct position along that path. This lets the explorer see how far the rover has gone over its mission.

VR experience. For VR, we used the route within Ingenuity’s range as our sample. This keeps the experience focused on a region of Mars that is well documented by NASA, and lets the explorer walk through the same terrain where the rover and the helicopter operated together. The VR version brings the whole project into one place: the terrain at different resolutions, the atmosphere layer, and the Bunsen Peak site. 

Benefits and intended impact:  The project lets anyone see and walk real Martian terrain at human scale, with the rover’s real path and measured atmospheric conditions in the same place. It is meant to make Mars data easier to explore and understand, and to show how a person on foot could plan a route across the surface. Pon eso y que también se quiere por si en otro momento se investiga la viabilidad del vida en otros planetas 

Tools, languages and hardware. Python (data processing, route planning and scene generation), Godot with GDScript (viewer and VR), pytest and Godot headless tests, and VR through Godot’s XR mode, targeting the Steam Frame headset. Data from NASA, USGS and ESA. We used Claude through the VS Code extension and the chat to support development, as declared in the usage documentation below. 

What makes it creative. It combines datasets of very different resolutions in one walkable scene. It recreates a real sample site, including the drill hole at full scale from the rover’s own drilling data. It also presents the atmosphere through a panel, false-color views, haze and sound, so the explorer can see, hear and read the conditions at their location.

Factors we considered. Detail against performance, so the highest resolution is used only at the point of interest. Scientific accuracy against approximation: everything that is synthetic or approximate is labeled in the data and limitations sections. Walkability, using slope thresholds and a suit factor in the route cost. And a VR experience limited to a well-documented region of Mar
